learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands the conditions that an electromechanical system must meet to convert energy via a magnetic field.
Knows that the properties of electrical machines are largely determined by the distribution of the magnetic field in the air gap of the machine.
Knows the construction and principle of operation of synchronous generators as the basic source of electrical energy in the national power system.
Knows what determines and how to obtain the required course of electromotive force induced in the generator windings and under what conditions this course is maintained after loading the generator.
Knows how to ensure the required quality of electrical energy generated by a stand-alone generator.
Knows the basic operational and control properties of synchronous generators and motors, including power factor control principles.
Knows the construction and principle of operation of three-phase induction machines as a basic drive element.
Knows the basic operational and control properties of induction motors, including speed control principles and starting methods.
Knows the construction, principle of operation, and equivalent circuit of a single-phase transformer.
Knows the construction and specific operation of typical commutator machines with a single brush system.
Can write and calculate energy and co-energy for a simple electromechanical system.
Can determine the field distribution in the air gap of a typical electrical machine for a given winding distribution and can consciously shape the distribution of this field.
Can calculate fluxes coupled with windings and their inductances, also as functions of the position of the moving part of the machine, in particular the rotor.
Can write the dynamic equations of the circuit model of an electromechanical energy converter and determine its parameters for simple designs.
Can determine the state coordinates (operating point) of a synchronous machine in a steady state.
Can determine the state coordinates (operating point) of an induction machine in a steady state.
Can use data from the nameplate and catalog of a transformer to determine its operational properties.
Can write and understand the origin of equations describing the dynamics of commutator machines with a single brush system.
Can use general principles of energy conversion to formulate dynamic equations of a simple electromechanical system.
The student can work in a group and cooperate with it in carrying out a research topic in a computer laboratory.
The student can prepare a report and documentation of the performed tests, appropriately process the results and draw conclusions.

syllabus_topics: Numerical calculations performed in a computer laboratory, preceded by data preparation for simulation and concluded with a discussion of calculation results: 1. Simple linear motion energy converter: writing motion equations, analyzing magnetic field distribution, analytically determining motion equation parameters, simulating converter operation (3 hours).
2. Rotary motion energy converter: writing motion equations, analyzing magnetic field distribution, analytically determining motion equation parameters, simulating converter operation (2 hours).

3. Elementary windings of rotary electrical machines: application of flux function and continuity law to determine the distribution of magnetic field intensity and induction in the machine's air gap, calculating fluxes and inductances of single coils and forces and moments associated with them (4 hours).
4. Windings of rotating field electrical machines: calculating coupled fluxes, winding inductances, and electromagnetic moments in winding systems (3 hours).

5. Three-phase synchronous machine: selection of generator armature winding to obtain the required electromotive force waveform, using 0dq model equations for steady-state calculations of a standalone generator and a machine cooperating with a rigid network. Construction of the synchronous machine phasor diagram (4 hours).

6. Three-phase induction machine: using the machine's equivalent circuit to calculate currents and torque in various operating states and to determine the current and torque dependence on speed, determining the mechanical characteristic and current dependence on speed, motor speed control, and efficiency determination (4 hours).
7. Single-phase transformer: determining equivalent circuit parameters (2 hours).
8. DC commutator machine: using dynamic equations for steady-state calculations, simulating dynamic states (4 hours).
9. Two control tests (4 hours).

THEORETICAL BASICS OF ELECTROMECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERTER OPERATION 1. Construction and properties of magnetic circuits of electromechanical energy converters, considering the nonlinearity of the magnetization characteristic and the influence of the air gap on circuit parameters (2 hours).

2. Single-phase transformer as an example of magnetically coupled windings, considering the influence of magnetization characteristic nonlinearity and leakage flux. Single-phase transformer construction, transformer parameters, equivalent circuit and identification of its parameters, short-circuit voltage (3 hours).

3. Conditions for electromechanical energy conversion – requirements for converter designs, energy conservation principle, electromagnetic induction law, energy and co-energy of nonlinear and linear magnetically coupled winding systems, methods for calculating forces and moments in electromechanical energy converters (3 hours).
4. General principles of electromechanical energy conversion: Hamilton's principle of least action, Lagrange function, Euler-Lagrange equations (2 hours).

5. Construction of rotary electromechanical energy converters – magnetic circuit elements, spatial distribution of winding coils, purpose of this distribution. Magnetic field in the air gap of a rotary electromechanical energy converter – calculation method: flux law and function, unit air gap permeance function, flux continuity law, distribution of magnetic field intensity and induction in the gap (2 hours).

6. Parameters of circuit equations of electromechanical energy converters – winding inductances, flux coupled with winding - calculation method, considering winding distribution when calculating flux coupled with winding (2 hours).
7. Rotating field in AC electromechanical energy converters, methods of generation and shaping (2 hours).

CONSTRUCTION AND PROPERTIES OF BASIC ELECTRICAL MACHINES 8. Three-phase AC synchronous generators – construction of a generator with a cylindrical rotor, principle of operation, phasor diagram, equivalent circuit, armature reaction reactance, leakage reactance, synchronous reactance. Conditions under which three-phase AC (sinusoidal) voltages are generated and their shape maintained in a loaded generator (2 hours).

9. Cylindrical synchronous machine cooperating with the power grid in steady state – rotating field, phasor diagram, power angle, motor and generator operation, power factor control, V-curves (2 hours).

10. Three-phase induction machines – construction, types, motor operation principle, slip definition. Description of an induction machine supplied from a symmetrical 3-phase network at constant rotational speed in steady state – equivalent circuit, mechanical characteristic equation and waveform for typical machines, range of motor, generator, and braking operation. Additional conditions for energy conversion in an induction machine, speed control, problems and starting methods, individual losses and efficiency (4 hours).

11. Machines with mechanical commutator – construction, rotor windings, role of the commutator in creating the rotor's magnetic configuration. Dynamic equations of a machine with one pair of brushes. Basic types of DC commutator machines – additional conditions for energy conversion, mechanical characteristics of series and separately excited motors, speed control, problems and starting methods. AC series commutator motors (universal). Additional conditions for energy conversion in commutator machines (4 hours).

assessment_methods.method: Completion of laboratory classes (including two control tests)

assessment_rules: To obtain a positive final grade, it is necessary to receive a positive grade from the laboratory-auditory exercises and pass the exam. Detailed conditions for passing the laboratory-auditory exercises are determined by the instructor, with a positive grade required for two control tests.
